used.how: its 'host thread' lever for the engram lookup is what P.6 builds; begin_chunk's host time is on the wall of a host-bound chunk, so the worker overlaps it with layer dispatch
numba launches from the new worker thread go through engram_bfp8._run, which keeps torch's thread count; perf_engram_host.py already checks a launch from another thread

missing: testing/host_transfers.py wraps ttnn module attributes process-wide: a transfer a background thread issues for begin_chunk counts against whichever layer the main thread is in; the worker calls copy_host_to_device_tensor through a reference bound at import
MeshDevice has no Python binding for its CQ count (num_hw_cqs); the harness and tt-d-gen open one CQ

ttnn.to_device does not release the GIL; copy_host_to_device_tensor does. tensor_from_bfp8_bytes + .tobytes() hold the GIL for ~35 ms a 5120-token layer (two 33 MB copies); a host tensor's shard bytes are writable in place through torch.from_dlpack(host.host_buffer().get_shard(coord))

P.6's gate command sets BRINGUP_PROFILE_WALL=1 on test_profile.py, so gate.with_clean_wall adds no profiled run and device_ms_total is always MISSING; the gate needs the plain profiled run as a second segment (tasks.yaml)

overseer.evidence: no padding or inflated work: the same rows and bytes, only moved to a worker thread (tt/perf_engram_async.py: device bytes equal to the off path's)
